name: codeql-format-string-requires-separate-args
hook: CodeQL format-string alerts need separate console.error args
body:
CodeQL flags console.error(`message ${userData}`, error) as a format-string vulnerability because an attacker who controls `userData` could inject format specifiers (%s, %d, etc.) to read/write stack memory. The fix is to pass user-controlled values as separate arguments: console.error('message', userData, ':', error) — this is safe because console methods treat subsequent args as data, not format strings.

**Why:** This is the second CodeQL format-string fix task (after #2242), confirming the pattern is recurring. Both were triggered by the same underlying issue: multiple developers using template literals with dynamic data in error logging.

**How to apply:** When CodeQL reports a format-string alert on console.error/warn/log, convert template literals to separate arguments. Search for `console\.error\(\`.*\$\{` across the codebase whenever addressing this type of alert.
why: Without this fix, CodeQL will fail on the dev branch, blocking merges. Format-string vulnerabilities can be exploited to read sensitive data from stack memory.
